problem: State-centric scene graphs used for multimodal lifelong navigation cannot distinguish same-category instances, keep semantic targets and exploration frontiers as separate inputs, and do not record navigation history or reuse cross-subtask experience, causing instance confusion, repeated exploration and lost verified targets.
motivation: Multimodal lifelong navigation (object, language and image goals in sequence) is event-driven: each decision changes the agent's spatial knowledge and the experience available later. A representation that grounds queries to instances, unifies targets with frontiers, and keeps trajectory and outcome memory should make VLM-based decisions more reliable.
key_idea: Extend the scene graph into a spatio-temporal event graph, with a spatial axis of query-conditioned instance grounding plus occupancy-aware frontier nodes and a temporal axis of short-term trajectory and long-term verified-outcome memory, so a VLM selects an object or frontier node.
insight: The cumulative ablation on a 36-episode GOAT-Bench subset shows every component adds SR: scene graph 45.7 to 55.8, QIG to 59.4, OFG to 66.9 (largest gain), DWM to 70.9. Error analysis shows total failures fall from 123 to 81, instance confusion from 13 to 6, and inefficient exploration from 45 to 27, while execution/stopping failures barely change (18 to 14), so the gains are in high-level reasoning rather than low-level control.
method: Query-Conditioned Instance Grounding (QIG): a VLM category prefilter keeps up to 20 nodes, CLIP pre-ranks them, and a VLM scores relevance and writes a query-conditioned description per candidate; the top instances become query-instance edges for image and language queries, while object queries are not pruned.

Occupancy-Aware Frontier Grounding (OFG): frontier cells are clustered into frontier nodes with center, reachability, geodesic path cost, exploration gain and visitation state, linked to nearby semantic anchors and to the agent by navigation edges, so objects and frontiers live in one graph.

Short-term decision-trajectory window: keeps the latest 20 executed decisions with compact trajectory segments (endpoints, traversed nodes, coverage, outcome), projected onto the graph to mark visited frontiers and repeated paths as soft evidence, and cleared after each subtask.

Long-term task-event window: stores up to 8 anchors of VLM-verified successes (no simulator GT) holding instance ID, category, modality, query, appearance feature and room; these are re-associated to live nodes via ID or CLIP similarity (0.92/0.70 thresholds) with a VLM verifier for ambiguous cases.

Event-graph VLM policy: the serialized graph (query, agent, objects, frontiers, relations, recent events) is fed to GPT-5.4-mini, which outputs an Object, Frontier or earlier-Image choice, and a stop-verification prompt checks success.
Perception and mapping: YOLOv8x-World, SAM-L and CLIP ViT-H build a 3D scene graph and a TSDF occupancy map from 7 RGB-D headings per step, with an adaptive step budget B = max(50, floor(2 sqrt(A))).

setting.backbone: gpt-5.4-mini (frozen VLM) with YOLOv8x-World, SAM-L, CLIP ViT-H-14
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D, 7 headings 40° apart per high-level step (120° HFOV), with pose
setting.action_space: high-level selection of an object node or frontier node, executed via a planner along occupancy-derived paths with 1.0 m motion horizon
setting.privileged: none (no simulator semantic labels or GT goal positions; verification uses VLM, not GT)

numbers.extra: training-free; step budget max(50, floor(2 sqrt(A)))

results: On GOAT-Bench Val-Unseen STEGNav reaches 66.3 SR / 39.7 SPL, beating MSGNav (62.4 SR, no SPL reported) by 3.9 SR and EvoMemNav (59.6/38.9) by 6.7 SR / 0.8 SPL. On HM3Dv1 and HM3Dv2 it obtains the best SR (64.0 and 69.4) but lower SPL than EvoMemNav (29.8 vs 33.6, 28.2 vs 39.4).
limitations: SPL on HM3D ObjectNav is below EvoMemNav, so higher success does not translate into shorter paths.
Low-level execution and stopping errors remain a main residual failure source and are not addressed by the graph representation.
Relies on many proprietary VLM calls per step (GPT-5.4-mini for prefilter, grounding, selection and verification); ablations use only a 36-episode subset.
